newsitem.title: USA: Republicans score well in Texas races.
newsitem.headline: Republicans score well in Texas races.

text.p: Republicans scored well in Texas in the U.S. congressional elections on Tuesday, picking up two House of Representatives seats left open by retiring Democrats and posting a comfortable win in the state's Senate race.
Republican candidates gained two House seats in Dallas and Fort Worth where U.S. Reps. John Bryant and Pete Geren -- both Democrats -- decided not to seek re-election.
In the Dallas seat, Republican candidate Pete Sessions scored 53 percent support to beat his Democratic rival John Pouland.
In Fort Worth, Republican nominee Kay Granger thrashed Democratic candidate Hugh Parmer by 17 percentage points.

In another closely-watched House race, Republican Ron Paul -- a former Libertarian Party presidential candidate who has advocated legalising drugs -- appeared headed toward a narrow victory over Democrat Charles "Lefty" Morris in a seat being vacated by Democrat-turned-Republican Greg Laughlin.
Laughlin lost to Paul in last spring's Republican primary.

Freshman Republican Steve Stockman, whom Democrats had considered vulnerable, looked to be on his way to a runoff with Democratic challenger Nick Lampson after neither garnered 50 percent of the vote in an open contest.
Also facing a runoff was Ken Bentsen, a Democratic incumbent in Houston and nephew of former Sen. Lloyd Bentsen.
Republicans had hoped to push both the Stockman and Bentsen races into a Dec. 10 runoff and party leaders said they were now optimistic of winning both.

The runoffs, unprecedented in Texas, were made possible by a controversial redrawing of 13 congressional districts when the Supreme Court earlier this year ruled the Democratic-controlled state legislature had gerrymandered the boundaries of three districts on racial lines.
The changes immediately raised Republican hopes in several tight races. Their gains here were expected to help prevent Democrats from regaining control of the House.

Rubbing salt in the wounds of Texas Democrats, Republican Sen. Phil Gramm easily won re-election over schoolteacher Victor Morales. Gramm spent millions on a campaign in which he branded Morales, who campaigned out of his family's pickup truck, a free-spending liberal.
